pathogen_scientific_name.quote: the bacterium Xanthomonas albilineans causes leaf scald

type_of_disease.quote: the bacterium Xanthomonas albilineans causes leaf scald

affected_parts.quote: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf... Ultimately, the entire plant dies.

summary.value: A white 1-2 mm 'pencil line' on the leaf running parallel to the veins from midrib to margin with a diffuse yellow border, progressing to brown necrosis from the leaf tip or margin with inward-curling, scalded-looking leaves and eventual plant death.
summary.quote: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf. This line extends from the midrib to the leaf margin running parallel to the veins. A diffuse yellow border of varying widths runs parallel to the pencil line. The pencil line may have areas of reddish discoloration along part of its length. As the disease progresses, brown, dead tissue (necrosis) develops from the leaf tip or leaf margin and eventually extends the entire leaf. Leaves look burned and curl inward, giving them a scalded appearance–hence the disease's name. Ultimately, the entire plant dies.

diagnostic_features.value: A narrow white 'pencil line' (1-2 mm wide) extending from midrib to leaf margin parallel to veins, bordered by a diffuse yellow margin, sometimes with reddish discoloration, leading to burned-looking, inward-curling scalded leaves.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Eyespot disease is caused by the fungus Bipolaris sacchari .

type_of_disease.quote: Eyespot disease is caused by the fungus Bipolaris sacchari .

affected_parts.quote: The first observable symptoms are minute water-soaked spots that usually occur on young leaves

summary.value: Minute water-soaked spots appear first on young leaves, developing into reddish-brown elliptical lesions with yellowish-brown margins, often accompanied by long reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks (runners) extending toward the leaf tip in cooler conditions.
summary.quote: The first observable symptoms are minute water-soaked spots that usually occur on young leaves (Comstock and Steiner 1989). Typical mature eyespot symptoms are characterized by a reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins (Figure 1). Reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks, sometimes called "runners," extend upward from individual lesions toward the leaf tip.

diagnostic_features.value: Reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins, with reddish-brown to yellowish-brown 'runners' (streaks 3–6 mm wide and 30–90 cm long) extending upward from lesions toward the leaf tip in cooler temperatures.
diagnostic_features.quote: Typical mature eyespot symptoms are characterized by a reddish-brown elliptical lesion (0.5–4.0 mm long, 0.5–2.0 mm wide) with yellowish-brown margins (Figure 1). Reddish-brown to yellowish-brown streaks, sometimes called "runners," extend upward from individual lesions toward the leaf tip. These streaks are 3–6 mm wide and 30–90 cm long.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) is a distinct member of the Polerovirus genus of the Luteoviridae family.

type_of_disease.quote: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) is a distinct member of the Polerovirus genus of the Luteoviridae family.

affected_parts.quote: The YLD affected sugarcane plants exhibited various symptoms including mild to severe yellowing of the midribs (Fig. 1B and C), smaller and clustering of leaves at the crown region of the plant along with the shortened internodes. Midrib yellowing (Fig. 1D and E), necrosis observed from tip to the base of leaves. Subsequently, complete drying of leaf foliage with stunted and poor growth was observed due to severe incidence of the disease under field situations

summary.value: YLD-affected plants show mild to severe yellowing of the midribs, smaller and clustered leaves at the crown, shortened internodes, necrosis from tip to base of leaves, and eventual complete drying of foliage with stunted, poor growth.
summary.quote: The YLD affected sugarcane plants exhibited various symptoms including mild to severe yellowing of the midribs (Fig. 1B and C), smaller and clustering of leaves at the crown region of the plant along with the shortened internodes. diagnostic_features.value: Midrib yellowing (mild to severe) is a hallmark sign, accompanied by smaller and clustered leaves at the crown region and shortened internodes; young leaves show bright midrib yellowing while matured leaves show extensive discoloration of lamina with necrosis.
diagnostic_features.quote: matured leaves with mild yellowing of midrib (B); young leaves showing mild midrib yellowing and matured leaves showing initial discoloration of leaf lamina (C); young leaves showing bright midrib yellowing and matured leaves showing extensive discoloration of lamina with necrosis (D); severe necrosis of leaf area in matured leaves (E) and plant showed extensive stunting with complete drying (F)

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV), and Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) (Rott et al., 2000; Viswanathan and Rao, 2011) are associated with mosaic disease

type_of_disease.quote: Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV), and Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) (Rott et al., 2000; Viswanathan and Rao, 2011) are associated with mosaic disease
The fungus is soil-borne and enters through cut ends and proliferates rapidly in the parenchymatous tissues.

affected_parts.quote: Fungus enters cut ends, turning tissues red and then black with a pineapple smell. Buds and roots fail, plants dieback or are stunted with low sugar content.

summary.value: Infection of sugarcane setts at cut ends causes tissues to first redden, then turn brownish-black/black; severely affected setts show internodal cavities covered with mycelium and abundant spores; a characteristic pineapple smell accompanies the rotting tissues; buds and roots fail and plants dieback or are stunted.
summary.quote: The affected tissues first develop a reddish colour which turns to brownish black in the later stages. The severely affected setts show internodal cavities covered with the mycelium and abundant spores. A characteristic pineapple smell is associated with the rotting tissues.

diagnostic_features.value: A characteristic pineapple smell associated with rotting tissues; internodal cavities covered with mycelium and abundant spores; cut ends turn red then black.
diagnostic_features.quote: A characteristic pineapple smell is associated with the rotting tissues.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sugarcane smut is caused by the dimorphic basidiomycetous fungus S. scitamineum (Sydow) M. Piepenbr., M. Stoll & Oberw. (Syn: Ustilago scitamiea H. & P. Sydow).

type_of_disease.quote: Sugarcane smut is caused by the dimorphic basidiomycetous fungus S. scitamineum

affected_parts.quote: Whip smut is basically a disease of meristematic tissues, and the pathogen only propagates in young and actively growing plant tissues... It enters the healthy sugarcane plant through lateral buds, in a very characteristic manner, i.e., by producing a typical black whip

summary.value: Infected plants are usually stunted in growth and produce thin slender canes with broad-spaced nodes, having a whip-like sorus either at the top of affected stalks or on the side shoots of standing canes; grass-like shoots with small and narrow leaves appear early, and long black whip-like structures appear at the stalk tip with longer whips curving downwards.
summary.quote: The infected sugarcane plants are usually stunted in growth and produce thin slender canes, generally with broad-spaced nodes, having a whip-like sorus either at the top of affected stalks or on the side shoots of standing canes

diagnostic_features.value: Emergence of a 'smut whip' — a typical black whip-like sorus — is the most identifiable diagnostic feature of infected plants.
diagnostic_features.quote: Sugarcane smut is characterized by the emergence of a typical structure, called "smut whip", the most identifiable diagnostic feature of infected plants

conflicts.note: Ustilago scitaminea is a synonym; Sporisorium scitamineum is the current accepted name per peer-reviewed literature (PMC8703903).

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Pathogenicity assay confirmed that F. verticillioides was directly responsible for disease on sugarcane.

type_of_disease.quote: Identification and Characterization of Pathogenic and Endophytic Fungal Species Associated with Pokkah Boeng Disease of Sugarcane

affected_parts.quote: The usual symptoms include red streaking, chlorosis, malformation, and stalk rot.

summary.value: Malformed or twisted leaves near the shoot apex with wrinkling, twisting and shortening, chlorosis at the leaf base, red streaking, and in severe cases dark red streaks and ladder-like lesions inside the stalk and rind with a 'knife-cut' lesion in the rind and top rot.
summary.quote: Malformed or twisted leaves occur near the shoot apex. Young leaves may exhibit pronounced wrinkling, twisting and shortening. Chlorosis (yellowing) is often evident at the leaf base, and necrosis may develop. Spindle infection can spread into the stalk. In severe cases, dark red streaks and ladder-like lesions form inside the stalk and the rind. A "knife-cut" lesion may form in the rind.

diagnostic_features.value: Three-phase progression: (1) chlorotic patches at base of young leaves with wrinkled/twisted/shortened leaves; (2) top rot phase with red specks dissolved and rotten/dried spindle base; (3) knife cut stage showing transverse cuts in the rind of the stalk; also dark red streaks and ladder-like lesions inside stalk.
diagnostic_features.quote: The disease develops in three major phases. The earliest symptoms are the appearance of chlorotic patches towards the base of young leaves... Leaves are wrinkled, twisted and shortened... The top rot phase is the most serious stage where the malformation and twisting of leaves are pronounced. Red specks are dissolved and the whole base of the spindle gets rotten and dried up... The third stage known as the knife cut stage shows transverse cuts in the rind of the stalk or stem.

conflicts.note: Plantix lists Fusarium moniliforme; the PMC peer-reviewed study confirmed F. verticillioides (teleomorph Gibberella fujikuroi) as the pathogenic species via pathogenicity assay.
LSU AgCenter uses the teleomorph name Gibberella fujikuroi; the current accepted anamorph name is Fusarium verticillioides.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The disease is caused by a phytoplasma .

type_of_disease.quote: The disease is caused by a phytoplasma .

affected_parts.quote: Leaves become pale yellow to completely chlorotic, thin and narrow. The plants appear bushy and 'grass-like' due to reduction in the length of internodes premature and continuous tillering.

summary.value: Affected plants produce numerous lanky tillers from the base with pale yellow to chlorotic, thin, narrow leaves, giving a bushy 'grass-like' appearance due to shortened internodes and continuous tillering.
summary.quote: The disease is characterised by the production of numerous lanky tillers from the base of the affected shoots. Leaves become pale yellow to completely chlorotic, thin and narrow. The plants appear bushy and 'grass-like' due to reduction in the length of internodes premature and continuous tillering.

diagnostic_features.value: Numerous lanky tillers from the base, pale yellow to chlorotic thin narrow leaves, bushy grass-like appearance with shortened internodes, stunted clumps with premature proliferation of auxillary buds, and canes (if formed) with aerial roots at lower nodes and papery abnormally elongated buds.
diagnostic_features.quote: The affected clumps are stunted with premature proliferation of auxillary buds. Cane formation rarely occurs in the affected clumps, if formed, thin with shorter internodes having aerial roots at the lower nodes. The buds on such canes usually papery and abnormally elongated.

type_of_disease.quote: Once a variety becomes susceptible, rust can be controlled with the application of fungicide.

affected_parts.quote: Small chlorotic areas appear on the leaves at first as flecks.

summary.value: Small chlorotic flecks on leaves that elongate into reddish-brown lesions, sometimes with a yellow halo, with pustules erupting on the lower leaf surface releasing reddish-brown spores.
summary.quote: Small chlorotic areas appear on the leaves at first as flecks. Later, the flecks elongate and become reddish-brown. The spots continue to enlarge with a slight yellow halo surrounding the lesion on some varieties. The lesion takes on a pustular appearance on the lower surface of the leaf and pustules erupt, releasing a reddish-brown mass of spores.

diagnostic_features.value: Pustular appearance on the lower surface of the leaf with pustules erupting to release a reddish-brown mass of spores; heavily infected leaves dry out and die prematurely on susceptible varieties.
diagnostic_features.quote: The lesion takes on a pustular appearance on the lower surface of the leaf and pustules erupt, releasing a reddish-brown mass of spores. On susceptible varieties, heavily infected leaves dry out and die prematurely.
